name: Probiotics for body odor
lead: Probiotics for body odor is the idea that taking probiotic microbes, or shifting the gut or skin microbiome, changes how a person smells, so that they come across as fresher and cleaner in close contact. People who try it are looking for an internal route to a better scent profile alongside deodorant and hygiene.

Body odor arises mainly from bacteria on the skin breaking down sweat-gland secretions, especially from the apocrine glands in the armpits, with genes, diet and health contributing; Wikipedia lists the gut microbiome as a factor that can affect it, but its article does not mention probiotics [1]. Research on the armpit microbiota describes how skin bacteria convert odorless secretions into volatile odorous molecules [3], and a 2022 review describes probiotic modulation of the skin microbiome as an emerging area for conditions including acne, body odour and atopic dermatitis [4].
Reference sources also note a 2020 study on cutaneous bacteria in the gut microbiome as biomarkers of systemic malodor [1]. No human trial of oral probiotics for ordinary body odor was located.

paras: Bacteria on the skin cause most body odor by breaking down secretions from skin glands. Apocrine glands in the armpits release compounds that skin bacteria convert into odorous molecules; Corynebacterium, Staphylococcus hominis, propionibacteria and S. epidermidis are among the species described as contributing, and genetics also plays a role [1]. Diet can change how sweat smells; one study cited by Wikipedia found that men who ate more fruits and vegetables had sweat judged more pleasant [1].

A 2013 review of the axillary microbiota describes sequencing studies of its composition and notes that the physiological activity of an individual microbiota remains largely unknown, proposing metatranscriptomics to link specific bacterial activities to individual differences in odor [3].
Wikipedia describes antiperspirants, deodorants and daily washing with antibacterial soap as standard measures, along with surgery for severe sweating in rare cases [1].

A 2022 review in Probiotics and Antimicrobial Proteins presents the skin microbiome as a target for probiotic intervention and lists body odour among the microbially influenced conditions of interest to dermatology and cosmetic research [4]. A 2021 study in Scientific Reports tested a product made by fermenting Lotus corniculatus seed with Lactobacillus acidophilus KNU-02 and reported it reduced axillary malodor and affected the axillary microbiota; the tested material was a fermented plant product rather than a live probiotic [5].
No studies found of oral probiotic supplements for ordinary body odor. Related research on the armpit microbiota, skin probiotics and a fermented-extract deodorant is described above [3][4][5].

card.summary: Probiotics are floated for body odor via the gut-skin link; no human trials were found.
card.note: Gut-microbiome link is a research observation, not a tested treatment.

quick.overview:
Some people propose probiotics to change body odor through the gut microbiome. A 2020 study explored skin bacteria in the gut microbiome as markers of systemic malodor.

No trials of probiotics for body odor were found in the sources consulted.
quick.mechanism: The proposed route is the gut microbiome influencing what is excreted through skin. This is not shown by trials in the sources consulted.
quick.risks: Not assessed in the sources consulted.

chain: Probiotic taken by mouth or applied to skin
Shift in gut or skin microbial community
Possible change in odor-producing bacteria and body scent
angle.text: Users hope that changing the microbes in the gut or on the skin will reduce odor-causing bacterial activity and make their natural scent less pronounced.
